page: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.24xlarge is an x86_64 high-performance computing server powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. It features 48 physical cores and 48 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz with a single thread per core configuration. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing 16.0 GB of RAM per core. It utilizes the AWS Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or integrated GPUs. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 150 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU physics tests scoring in the top 10% of all servers. The DDR5 memory subsystem delivers exceptional throughput, achieving top-tier ratings in large-block uncached read (695.05 GB/sec) and write (347.3 GB/sec) operations. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation with Clang also rank in the top 10%. Single-core performance remains strong, placing in the top 25% across stress-ng and Geekbench tests.

From a resource density perspective, the server offers a highly efficient allocation of high-speed DDR5 memory relative to dedicated physical cores, making it highly cost-effective for memory-bound parallel processing. However, the lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs for disk-heavy operations. The absence of GPU acceleration limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, though it maintains strong performance in CPU-based LLM inference and Redis SET operations.

This instance is optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) workloads, including computational fluid dynamics, weather forecasting, molecular dynamics, and large-scale scientific simulations. It is also highly suitable for memory-intensive database operations, parallel software compilation, and high-throughput network applications.
